nar.text: During the entire night heavy rain showers had come down, causing damage to parts of the circuit.
Ingegnere Vittorio Jano anticipated rain during the race and ordered the Alfa mechanics to add front fenders to the racing cars of Nuvolari, Borzacchini and Campari.
The drivers were released at five-minute intervals.
At 8:30 AM, under a blue sky and the sun shining, Varzi in the red #2 Bugatti started first.
Castagna stopped his blue Salmson after only 19 kilometers just before Caltavutoro.
After just 50 kilometers near Castellana at the bottom of a steep hill just before a bridge, Fagioli raced into a parapet, tearing up the rear axle of his Maserati.
The Sicilian, Magistri, retired his Alfa Romeo in the mountains when his car broke a timing gear.
Varzi completes lap one in 2h03m54.8s, 70.700 km/h, with a safe lead.
Nuvolari stops to change two tyres as a precaution, losing 2m5s.
On the second lap slight rain began to fall, which then increased progressively.
Borzacchini stopped briefly to have spark plugs changed.
Biondetti, blinded by mud and rain, arrived too fast at a corner where his Maserati bounced against a wall
Varzi's second lap is ten minutes slower, including a stop for a plug and tyres; he still leads comfortably.
At the end of lap two, the middle of the race, all drivers stopped at their pits to refuel and change wheels.
Pellegrini retires his Alfa Romeo.
Nuvolari and Campari lost more time on the third lap while Borzacchini cut his time down by over two minutes.
Varzi keeps a two-minute advantage.
Piccolo retires, out of the time limit; Dreyfus, driving alone, retires with ignition problems.
After lap three, Varzi stopped for 1m50s at his pit to change one spark plug.
A stone hits Arcangeli in the left eye; Zehender takes over his car.
Campari stopped for just 54 seconds to have a loose mudguard tightened. Nuvolari stopped for only 43 seconds to change a spark plug.
Fog hung over some road sections, reducing visibility to barely 30 meters.
Varzi on the contrary struggled with mud splashed from the open front wheels; coating car, driver and mechanic.
The first to reach the finish on the road was Varzi, greeted with great applause.
The excitement of the crowd knew no boundaries when Nuvolari arrived at the finish under pouring rain, shortly thereafter followed by Borzacchini in second place.
Varzi had lost so much time on that last lap that he fell back to third place and was nearly caught by Campari in fourth place.
